subject: Banking
title: APIs as the New Banking Infrastructure
description: A fast breakdown of APIs as the New Banking Infrastructure for builders.

hook.text: Plaid connects 12,000 financial institutions to apps like Venmo and Robinhood.

buildup.text: An API is a digital connector. It lets one software system talk to another.

discovery.text: Visa tried to buy Plaid for $5.3 billion in 2020. The DOJ blocked it.

twist.text: Banks initially resisted APIs. Now they charge for premium API access.

climax.text: APIs transformed banking from a closed fortress into an open platform.

punchline.text: 12,000 banks connected by one API company. Plumbing is power.

quiz.question: Why did the DOJ block Visa's acquisition of Plaid?
options: Plaid was seen as a competitive threat to Visa's payment monopoly

details.summary: Application programming interfaces allow banks and fintech companies to connect their systems, enabling third-party developers to build products on top of bank infrastructure like accounts, payments, and identity verification.
details.whyItMatters: APIs are transforming banks from closed institutions into platforms that other companies build on. This shift lets innovation happen outside the bank, dramatically accelerating the pace of new financial product development.
takeaways: APIs let third parties access bank functions like payments and balances
Open banking regulations mandate API access in many countries
Banks become platforms that fintech companies build products upon

faq.question: What can developers build using banking APIs?
faq.answer: Payment apps, budgeting tools, lending platforms, account verification services, and more. Stripe uses bank APIs for payments, Plaid for account connections, and countless fintech apps for specific financial services.

faq.question: Are banking APIs secure?
faq.answer: Modern banking APIs use strong authentication, encryption, and token-based access. They are generally more secure than older methods like screen scraping where apps stored your bank password. Regulatory standards mandate security requirements.
